script: Messi bent this free kick seven meters. Here's how. Columbus, September. He's almost thirty meters out, near the sideline. From there, the goal looks just four degrees wide. And the wall stands right on the line to the post. A straight shot is impossible. So he doesn't hit it hard. He hits it off center, with about ten spins a second. That spin drags air around the ball. One side moves faster, the pressure drops, and the ball gets pushed sideways. Biblidom tracked it frame by frame. It leaves at about ninety kilometers an hour, clears the wall at two and a half meters, then curves seven meters into the corner. Without the spin, it lands seven meters short. Half a degree off, and it's wide. He's thirty-nine. And next week, he faces Columbus again, in the playoffs. Save this for your next free kick.
caption:
Messi bent this free kick 7 meters. 🎯

Columbus Crew vs Inter Miami, Sept 27: almost 30 m out, near the sideline, with the goal looking just 3.9° wide and a wall on the line to the post. A straight shot was impossible.

So he hit it off center, with about 10 spins a second. The spin bends the air around the ball (the Magnus effect) and the ball gets pushed sideways. It left at about 90 km/h, cleared the wall at 2.5 m and curved about 7 m into the corner. Without the spin, it lands 7 m short. Half a degree off, and it's wide.

Next up: Inter Miami vs Columbus Crew, MLS Cup Playoffs Game 1, Sat Nov 21 at Nu Stadium.
